title: Shortest Distance to a Character
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> ans: n entries → O(n) (returned output, not counted)
- int prev, int n: O(1) each
- not counted: input string s, returned vector ans
approach: For each position, the closest occurrence of c is either the nearest one to its left or the nearest one to its right. A left-to-right pass records the distance to the nearest c on the left using a running pointer to the last seen c. A right-to-left pass then takes the minimum of the existing value and the distance to the nearest c on the right. Both passes are O(n), giving O(n) total.
hints: For any position in the string, the nearest c must be either the closest one to its left or the closest one to its right. If you could compute, for every index, the distance to the nearest c on its left side only, what information would still be missing?

Two-pass array fill: a left-to-right pass stores the distance to the nearest c on the left, then a right-to-left pass takes the minimum with the nearest c on the right. For s = "loveleetcode", c = 'e': after the left pass, index 2 gets distance 14 (no e seen yet), which the right pass corrects to 1 (e at index 3).

```
prev = -infinity
for i from 0 to n-1:
    if s[i] == c: prev = i
    ans[i] = i - prev
prev = +infinity
for i from n-1 down to 0:
    if s[i] == c: prev = i
    ans[i] = min(ans[i], prev - i)
return ans
```

**c only at the end** - left pass alone cannot find right-side distances
`Input: s = "aab", c = "b"` → `Expected: [2,1,0]`
⚠️ Bug: only doing a left-to-right pass → returns [3,4,0] (indices 0 and 1 get sentinel-based distances)

**c only at the start** - right-pass sentinel must be large enough
`Input: s = "eab", c = "e"` → `Expected: [0,1,2]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing right-pass prev to n instead of 2*n → returns [0,1,1] (index 2 gets distance 1 from sentinel n=3 instead of 2 from c at index 0)

**Overwriting instead of taking min** - right pass must not discard left-pass results
`Input: s = "eabe", c = "e"` → `Expected: [0,1,1,0]`
⚠️ Bug: using `ans[i] = prev - i` instead of `ans[i] = min(ans[i], prev - i)` in the right pass → returns [0,2,1,0] (index 1 gets distance 2 from right-side e instead of 1 from left-side e)

**Left-pass sentinel too small** - prev must start before index 0
`Input: s = "ba", c = "a"` → `Expected: [1,0]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing left-pass prev to 0 instead of -n → returns [0,0] (index 0 gets distance 0 as if c were at index 0)

followUps.q: What if c is not guaranteed to occur in s?
followUps.a: Track a boolean `found` during the left pass. If no c was ever seen, return a vector of -1 for all positions. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if you need the distance to the k-th closest occurrence of c instead of the closest?
followUps.a: Collect all indices of c into a sorted array in one pass, then for each position binary search to find the k nearest indices. Time O(n log m) where m is the count of c, space O(m) for the index list.

followUps.q: What if there are multiple target characters and you need the distance to the closest of any of them?
followUps.a: Store the targets in a hash set, then the same two-pass approach works - update prev whenever s[i] is in the target set. Time O(n), space O(|targets|) for the set.
